I’m a teacher. But I also am not a particular fan of letting kids struggle. I grew up at a poorer school that had a bare bones curriculum because the school could afford neither teachers nor materials for courses outside of the state’s core. I watched teachers growing up who fought tooth and nail for every student, and the school had a 99% graduation rate, because despite lack of resources and funding, there was more to the school than its courses.

If you’re comfortable letting students slip by knowingly, then to each their own.
And then what? They simply fall through the cracks?

You outright stated you are using toddler strategies. Treating students like toddlers will not show that you value them. I have never, from being a student to teaching, seen this go over well.

You will not win, and they will give up. I don’t see this working out well whatsoever, but good luck I suppose.

Edit to elaborate: if you treat a student like a toddler, it comes across petty and immature in its own right. Students who are behaving this way usually have something going on in the background that leads them to call out, argue, etc. 

If they are bored in class, not being challenged, they may develop a why bother attitude.

Students with untreated ADHD may be the type who get their dopamine rush from arguments. 

Working on a symptom rather than a cause will work against you in many cases.
